questions.key_step: Tangent at P meets axis at (-x1,0); area = 1/(2m^3)
questions.justification: Single standard idea (T=0 and a right-triangle area), four short lines.

questions.key_step: Area = bc from tangent intercept; integer conditions on a
questions.justification: Subtangent plus a short integer-case check chained.

questions.key_step: Centroid sums give alpha, beta in terms of a; vertices on BC give p and a
questions.justification: Routine chain of linear equations; no idea beyond centroid.

questions.key_step: Circumcentre O so H=A+B+C, H on y-axis gives sum cos=0; then cos3 identity
questions.justification: Two ideas linked (orthocentre vector and x^3+y^3+z^3=3xyz with cos3x); not widely practised.

questions.key_step: alpha*beta = |9(cos+sin)^2-4|/2, extremum at the end of the range
questions.justification: Standard parametrisation of a diameter and a trig range.

questions.key_step: Tangents meet at (a t1t2, a(t1+t2)); only ratio of parameters matters
questions.justification: Standard parametric result applied once with a ratio condition.

questions.key_step: C2 on diagonal, sin(theta)=r/PC gives 30 degrees, tangent at 15 degrees to CB
questions.justification: Needs the corner-circle radius, an angle-from-tangent argument and tan 15; several linked steps.

questions.key_step: e^2=2(n+2)/(n+1) rational square forces n+1 odd perfect square
questions.justification: The number-theoretic reduction is the non-routine step; the rest is formula.

questions.key_step: Right angle in semicircle gives alpha; tangents perpendicular to radii; intersect
questions.justification: Several routine steps chained, no insight.

questions.key_step: OC perpendicular to CP gives OP^2=OC^2+r^2
questions.justification: One Pythagoras step after reading the area.

questions.key_step: Beta from common point, alpha from reflection of a point in the bisector
questions.justification: Reflection formula and a common-point observation; routine.

questions.key_step: Vertices from three lines, midpoint of AC, diagonal BD, distance
questions.justification: Pure computation with standard parallelogram facts.

questions.key_step: Two tangents and L3 give vertices; R=abc/4 Delta
questions.justification: Two tangent formulas plus circumradius; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Parametrise square by (t,1/t) and its 90-degree rotation; midpoint on curve gives 1/t^2-t^2=4
questions.justification: Idea of the rotated parametrisation is not routine; algebra then short.

questions.key_step: Half angle 30 degrees gives b/(ae)=1/sqrt3 and with LR gives a,b
Count multiples of a below (60-3a)/4 for each a, with strict inequality
questions.justification: Careful counting but simple; slip risk at a=4.

questions.key_step: On 4x+3y=75 z is quadratic in y; vertex lies in range
questions.justification: Reduction to a quadratic on the right edge; routine optimisation.
